answer: Map 6.3 shows low-carbon technology jobs concentrated in China’s east and southeast coastal manufacturing hubs—especially cities such as Guangzhou, Beijing, Shanghai, Suzhou, and Shenzhen—while fossil-fuel jobs are concentrated farther inland, especially around Shanxi and other north-central coal-mining areas. question: Inspect Map 6.3. Where in China are low-carbon technology jobs concentrated compared with fossil-fuel jobs?

events.query: "Map 6.3" low-carbon technology jobs fossil-fuel jobs China

results.text:
Map 6.3
Map 6.3. Title: "Low-carbon technology jobs in China are growing in manufacturing hubs on the southeast coast, whereas fossil fuel jobs are close to coal mines". Two side-by-side choropleth maps of China with province-level shading and red callout circles/boxes.

Panel a: "Share of online job postings related to low-carbon technologies, 2019". A choropleth map of China shaded from very light blue to dark blue, with a legend below labeled "Share of online job postings related to low-carbon technologies (%)" ranging from 0 to 7.90. The map labels neighboring regions/countries including RUSSIAN FEDERATION, MONGOLIA, DEM. PEOPLE'S REP. OF KOREA, REP. OF KOREA, MYANMAR, VIET NAM, LAO P.D.R., THAILAND, PHILIPPINES, and East China Sea. BEIJING is marked with a star. Red annotations highlight concentrations: a large red oval around the east coast/manufacturing belt with a red label pointing to it reading "East coast cities around Fujian, Guangdong, Beijing, and Shanghai"; two smaller red circles in the west/central area with a red label reading "Certain smaller cities including Huidong and Ganziz" (last word appears partly unclear in the page image). The panel emphasizes darker blue concentrations along the southeast/east coast and a few scattered inland hotspots.

Panel b: "Share of fossil fuel jobs, 2019". A choropleth map of China shaded from very light blue to dark blue, with a legend below labeled "Share of fossil fuel jobs (%)" ranging from 0 to 3.75. The same regional labels appear, including BEIJING marked with a star and East China Sea on the right. A large red oval highlights north-central China, with a red label "Shanxi province" pointing into the oval; a smaller red circle highlights the southwest with a red label "Western Guizhou". Darker blue concentrations are centered around Shanxi/north-central China and a smaller cluster in the southwest.

Source note beneath the figure: "Source: Park et al. 2023." Note: "In panel b, the share of fossil fuel jobs in 2019 is based on data from China Statistical Database, National Bureau of Statistics of China, Beijing, https://www.stats.gov.cn/english/." Figure credit on the map reads "IBRD 47928 | MARCH 2024".

uncertainties: The small red label in panel a appears to end with "Ganziz" or a similar place name; the final letters are difficult to read from the page image.
The map is reproduced at reduced size, so some province names and boundaries are visible only partially or not legibly; only clearly readable labels are transcribed.
